findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - A build started by an earlier Forge release receives a commit nudge. That release does not write `first_started_at` and overwrites `started_at` on each launch, so this fallback resets `elapsed` when the second launch starts. The earlier-release case in `tests/test_pane_data.py:155` changes only the version string while still running the new producer, so it cannot expose the reset.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - A worker asks a question and the person drops the fix while its checkout is retained, for example because it contains ignored local data. `forge fix drop` leaves the state marked `dropped` and preserves the thread record, but this scan does not exclude dropped states. The item therefore remains in `needs_you` even though it no longer waits for an answer.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - Available memory falls below Forge's admission floor while no run is queued. `_wait` at `src/forge/machine.py:272` will hold every new run, but this expression returns `busy: false`. Conversely, a test waiting only for a test-lane place makes it true even when a new build or review can start. This does not provide the machine-pressure flag specified for the pane's busy message.
findings.title: Report machine pressure in the busy field

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate. Case: normal use - The scheduled or manual Windows suite collects `tests` with `-m platform`. Python on Windows has no `resource` module, and pytest imports this file before applying the marker filter, so collection fails. After that is repaired, `tests/test_pane_data.py:192` also uses POSIX `shlex.join` for a command run through `cmd.exe`, so its platform-marked lending case cannot start the held test.
findings.title: Gate: Windows test collection and pane-data execution

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - The pane reads a remembered repo with 1,000 finished items and 50 active worktrees. The fixture creates those worktrees in the main repo, but registers only the ten other repos; their `fix/other` worktrees have no item state. `needs_you` consequently never scans the 50 active worktrees, so the timing and CPU assertions can pass even if scanning them exceeds the limits. The speed test also has no earlier-adopted repo case.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_pane_speed.py::test_4_forge_answers_the_pane_fast_small_and_cheap

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - A task worker asks a question, or the person runs tests while deciding how to answer a worker question. This proof creates worker questions only for fixes, and its concurrent test runs against a review stop rather than a question. Removing task-branch recognition or incorrectly hiding a question during its test run would leave the named proof passing.
